title: Syracuse Flock offboarding and Axon migration lifecycle
summary: Request #1903 advances the Syracuse transition with a dated revocation-to-removal lifecycle, a 13-reader city-property terminal inventory lead, and the separate 26-reader Axon contract era while preserving unresolved native audit, deletion, configuration, and migration evidence.

sources.title: Syracuse Common Council revokes contract with Flock
All Flock cameras in Syracuse have been removed
Syracuse police used Flock Safety readers for nearly a month after readers were supposed to be taken down

gaps: Native Flock terminal audit/deletion/credential/sharing records remain unresolved.
Serial-level inventory for the 13 city-property readers remains unresolved.
Native Axon contract/configuration and closed-system evidence remain unresolved.
No migration evidence for Flock data, hotlists, users, alerts, or cases was recovered.

data.question: What current public evidence establishes the Syracuse Flock offboarding lifecycle and boundary between the Flock and Axon network eras?
data.method: Reconciled six existing canonical Syracuse targets with City of Syracuse archives and March-July 2026 independent reporting.
data.framework: Contract revocation, platform use, physical removal, credential revocation, deletion, audit preservation, and replacement-vendor deployment are separate lifecycle states.
data.scope: Syracuse municipal Flock termination/removal and Axon replacement; city-property network only unless evidence identifies separate institutional assets.
findings: Syracuse Common Council revoked Flock's city access on March 23, 2026.
A city-imposed removal deadline was May 26, but independent reporting states Syracuse police continued using Flock readers for nearly a month after that deadline.
By July 2026 all 13 Flock readers on Syracuse city property were reported removed.
Syracuse separately approved 26 Axon readers under a five-year $422,000 agreement effective March 1, 2026.
City first-party archives preserve the March 23 Common Council meeting surface and the earlier Surveillance Technology Working Group ALPR review surface.
No reviewed evidence establishes migration of Flock hotlists, historical reads, users, credentials, case links, or alerts into Axon.
conclusions: Syracuse's Flock offboarding had distinct legal, operational, and physical-removal dates and should not be represented as one instantaneous termination event.
The city-property Flock terminal inventory is now bounded at 13 reported removed readers, subject to serial-level native inventory verification.
The Axon system is a separate vendor/network era and requires independent contract, retention, sharing, audit, and configuration verification.
recommendations: Recover final Flock Organization Audit, Network Audit, SharedNetworks, event, user/admin, configuration, deletion, credential-revocation, and support records.
Recover serial/location/removal/disposition records for all 13 city-property Flock readers.
Recover native Axon contract/procurement, 26 final locations, deployment state, retention, permissions, sharing, audit, integration, and termination terms.
Test the closed-system representation and any data/hotlist/user/case migration using native configuration and audit evidence.
counterarguments: Physical removal in July does not establish the date of platform disablement, credential revocation, deletion, or sharing-edge removal.
The 26-reader Axon authorization does not establish that all 26 were activated on the contract effective date.
limitations: This pass did not recover the native March 23 legislative instrument text, Flock terminal exports, Axon agreement attachment, or platform configuration exports.
unresolved: Who enabled national sharing and for what exact interval?
What searches occurred through the national-sharing exposure?
When were Flock accounts/API credentials and sharing edges actually revoked?
What was deleted, retained, exported, or placed under hold at offboarding?
Which 13 serials/locations were removed and when?
What exact Axon controls implement retention and Syracuse-only access?
Did any Flock data or identities migrate into Axon?
